145	/// Render a TOON list document from options.
146	///
147	/// # Errors
148	///
149	/// Returns an error if `rows`, `fields`, `hints`, or any row's value count
150	/// exceeds this module's hard size limits (`MAX_ROWS`, `MAX_FIELDS`,
151	/// `MAX_HINTS`) — an unbounded caller-supplied collection here would let a
152	/// single JS call force unbounded synchronous allocation on Node's event
153	/// loop, which `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` alone does not guard against. The
154	/// limits are checked on the JS arrays before anything is converted, and
155	/// the call's cells (at most 1,000,000) and string bytes (at most 64 MiB in
156	/// all, 1 MiB per cell or hint, 4 KiB for `typeName`, a field name or
157	/// `truncationHint`) are counted as they are read. Also
158	/// returns an error if `ToonOptions::validate()` rejects the input — a row
159	/// whose value count differs from `fields.len()`, a field name repeated in
160	/// `fields`, a reserved `type_name` (`totalCount`, `help`, `recovery` or `truncated`), or a
161	/// document over michi-core's shape caps. Any other type
162	/// or field name is valid and is quoted when TOON 4.4 §7.3 requires.
163	/// The error `reason` is `toon_validation_failed: ` followed by the `ToonError` Display text.
164	#[napi(catch_unwind, js_name = "renderToon", ts_args_type = "opts: ToonOptions")]

167	    let obj = input::object(opts, "opts")?;
168	    let rows = input::list_prop(&obj, "rows")?;
169	    let fields = input::list_prop(&obj, "fields")?;
170	    let hints = input::list_prop(&obj, "hints")?;
171	    input::check_len("rows", rows.len(), MAX_ROWS)?;
172	    input::check_len("fields", fields.len(), MAX_FIELDS)?;
173	    input::check_len("hints", hints.len(), MAX_HINTS)?;
174	    let opts = JsToonOptions {
175	        type_name: budget.string_prop(&obj, "typeName", "typeName", MAX_NAME_BYTES)?,
176	        total_count: input::typed_prop::<JsCount>(&obj, "totalCount")?,
177	        truncation_hint: budget.opt_string_prop(&obj, "truncationHint", "truncationHint", MAX_NAME_BYTES)?,
178	        fields: budget.strings(&fields, "fields", MAX_FIELDS, "field name", MAX_NAME_BYTES)?,
179	        hints: budget.strings(&hints, "hints", MAX_HINTS, "hint", MAX_STRING_BYTES)?,

185	/// The Rust-typed core of the `renderToon` export, for Rust callers that already hold a [`JsToonOptions`]. Applies
186	/// the same collection-length limits; the per-call byte budget only applies to the JS export, which enforces it
187	/// while converting.
188	///
189	/// # Errors
190	///
191	/// See the `renderToon` export ([`render_toon_js`]).
192	pub fn render_toon(opts: JsToonOptions) -> napi::Result<String> {
193	    if opts.rows.len() > MAX_ROWS {
194	        return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!("rows length {} exceeds maximum of {MAX_ROWS}", opts.rows.len())));
195	    }
196	    if opts.fields.len() > MAX_FIELDS {
197	        return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
198	            "fields length {} exceeds maximum of {MAX_FIELDS}",
199	            opts.fields.len()
200	        )));
201	    }
202	    if opts.hints.len() > MAX_HINTS {
203	        return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
204	            "hints length {} exceeds maximum of {MAX_HINTS}",
205	            opts.hints.len()
206	        )));
207	    }
208	
209	    let mut rows: Vec<Vec<crate::toon::Value>> = Vec::with_capacity(opts.rows.len());
210	    for row in opts.rows {
211	        if row.len() > MAX_FIELDS {
212	            return Err(napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
213	                "row length {} exceeds maximum fields per row of {MAX_FIELDS}",
214	                row.len()
215	            )));
216	        }
217	        rows.push(row.into_iter().map(js_value_to_rust).collect::<napi::Result<Vec<_>>>()?);
218	    }
219	
220	    let mut toon_opts = crate::toon::ToonOptions::new(opts.type_name, opts.fields, rows)
221	        .total_count(opts.total_count.map(JsCount::get))
222	        .hints(opts.hints);
223	    if let Some(hint) = opts.truncation_hint {
224	        toon_opts = toon_opts.truncation_hint(hint);
225	    }
226	
227	    crate::toon::render_toon(&toon_opts).map_err(|e| napi::Error::from_reason(format!("toon_validation_failed: {e}")))
228	}

## #3 [M] The NAPI 64 MiB cap limits input, not output: one response can produce about 1.2 GiB on the event loop

**Evidence.**
- The cap (`crates/michi-core/src/napi/input.rs:18`, `napi.rs:772-822`) charges caller bytes and storage, never the rendered size.
- Measured on the Rust API with one KV value of 1 MiB of U+0001: text render 6.0x (6,291,461 B), JSON 13.0x (13,631,654 B), and `to_call_tool_result` text plus `structured_content` 19.0x (19,923,115 B).
  - JSON is about 13x because the body is TOON `\u0001` re-escaped to `\\u0001` (7x), plus the raw `sections` copy (6x).
- A 1000-row table of 1000-char control strings (cells cut to 200 chars in text) gave 1.2 MB of text but 7.4 MB of JSON. `sections.rows` in JSON are uncapped by design (`docs/spec/03-rust-api.md:338`).
- Extrapolating to the cap (up to 64 KV calls of 1,000 x 1 MiB values each): about 384 MiB of text, 832 MiB of JSON, about 1.2 GiB in `toJSON`/`toCallToolResult`.
  - The NAPI `to_call_tool_result` (`napi.rs:1201-1228`) then parses `structured_content` into a `serde_json::Value` tree, so peak memory is higher still.
  - The `renderJson` result exceeds V8's maximum string length (about 2^29 code units). **Unverified end-to-end in Node:** I measured the ratios in Rust, not in a Node process.

**Why it matters.** The docs (`napi.rs:150-160`) justify the caps as stopping "unbounded synchronous allocation on Node's
event loop". A KV value is not truncated, and control characters expand 6-7x per escaping layer, so the bound is about
20x looser than stated. A tool that passes fetched text into `kvItems` lets the data's author pick the amplification.

**Proposed change.** Pick one:
- Charge each control character at its escaped size (6, or 13 for JSON) when accounting input.
- Or cap the rendered size per `render*`/`toCallToolResult` call (estimate it before rendering, return a `napi::Error` past e.g. 64 MiB).

Also state the amplification factor next to the 64 MiB figure. Add a Node test with a 1 MiB control-character value
asserting the output-size error.

**Effort:** M. **Breaking:** NAPI starts rejecting some inputs it accepts today. **Confidence:** high on the ratios,
medium on the end-to-end Node behaviour.
